purpose: An explicit scheme address is either well formed and parsed once, or refused with a typed reason. It never decays into token routing, and a prose URL never seeds a micronaut dispatch.

grammar.production: micronaut-uri = scheme '://' authority [ '/' path ] [ '?' query ] [ '#' fragment ]

scheme.case: input is lowercased; the canonical form is lowercase
scheme.percent_escapes: rejected (a scheme is not a percent-decoded component)

path.percent_escapes: validated and decoded exactly once before matching

token_boundary.start: the address ends at the first whitespace; the token before `://` scans back over non-space characters
token_boundary.trailing_punctuation_policy: stripped from the address, so a sentence-final `math://solve.` is the same address as `math://solve`
token_boundary.glued_prefix_policy: a glued prefix is folded into the scheme by the scan and refused as scheme_invalid; there is no silently-routed address hidden inside `x(math://…`
token_boundary.trailing_prose: words after the address are allowed: `math://solve algebra` is the address `math://solve` plus prose

compatibility.rule: the authority is folded into the leading path segment, so the historical shape `scheme://<op>` keeps meaning `op` while `scheme://<op>/<rest>` keeps parsing exactly as before

scheme_declaration.policy: the address participates in routing only when an active micronaut declares the scheme
scheme_declaration.prose_url_policy: a prose URL (`https://…`) is parsed, named in the diagnostic, and contributes no tokens to routing
declared_scheme_sources: entry id and its compatibility derivations

diagnostics.empty_reject_reason_means: either the address was accepted, or the request contained no `://` at all
diagnostics.uri_matched_means: the address itself selected at least one entry; a valid address that resolves to nobody falls back to prose routing and says so instead of pretending it matched

URI1.name: an_address_is_parsed_at_most_once
URI1.check: the single parser produces the scheme, authority, kind and operation consumed by matching

URI2.name: a_malformed_address_is_refused_by_name
URI2.check: every refusal carries one of reject_reasons

URI3.name: an_authority_is_required
URI3.check: scheme:// and scheme:///… are refused as authority_missing

URI4.name: percent_escapes_decode_exactly_once
URI4.check: sol%76e and solve are the same operation; an invalid escape is refused, never matched literally

URI6.name: a_prose_url_is_inert
URI6.check: an undeclared scheme yields scheme_not_declared and contributes no routing tokens

URI7.name: refusal_is_not_token_routing
URI7.check: a refused address scopes no candidates; the query still routes on its own tokens only

URI8.name: declared_schemes_are_authoritative
URI8.check: a declaring entry wins over a heavier derived-claim entry

URI9.name: derived_alias_collisions_are_refused
URI9.check: two derived claims with no declaration yield scheme_ambiguous

URI10.name: an_operation_is_matched_by_name
URI10.check: pattern_ops / template_ops membership decides, not catalogue non-emptiness

scheme_ownership.compatibility_source: entry id derivations (id, id-before-first-dash, id without -u/-agent)
scheme_ownership.precedence: a declaration settles ownership; entries that only derive the scheme do not compete with the declaring entry
scheme_ownership.compatibility_only: routes while exactly one entry derives the alias and nothing declares it; recorded as scheme_derived_compat:<scheme>
scheme_ownership.ambiguous: two or more entries derive the alias with no declaration to settle it: refused as scheme_ambiguous, never resolved by weight
scheme_ownership.declaration_requirement: every shipped track declares at least one `schemes` entry; no two tracks may declare the same address, and a shared derived alias is only safe when a declaration settles who owns it

known_ambiguous_umbrella_aliases.fold: FOLD-FIELD-u and FOLD-HOF-u both derive it; no track declares it, so fold:// is refused as scheme_ambiguous rather than routed by weight
known_ambiguous_umbrella_aliases.phil: PHIL-AI-u and PHIL-SELF-u both derive it; no track declares it, so phil:// is refused as scheme_ambiguous rather than routed by weight

pattern_operation_matching.policy: an operation is matched by name, never by the existence of a catalogue
pattern_operation_matching.fallback: the raw aiml_patterns / aiml_templates text may match the operation exactly (case-insensitive)
pattern_operation_matching.undeclared_result: no entry matches the address; the address resolves to nobody
pattern_operation_matching.removed_behaviour: an entry with any pattern or template used to accept every operation
